follow.description:
Which window a bar shows: "screen" = the last window of THIS bar's monitor's active
workspace (each screen shows its own) | "focus" = the focused window, whatever screen.

Takes "screen" or "focus". Default: "screen".

stripSuffix.description:
Drop what the app's mark already says: a title ending in " - Zen Browser" or
" — Visual Studio Code" (the window's initial title or the app's name, after one of
- — – | ·) is shown without it. A title is never stripped to nothing. true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

rewrites.description:
Regex rewrites of the shown title, in order: "re" is a JavaScript regex (written
without the slashes), "to" the replacement ($1 is the first group). A rule whose
regex is invalid is skipped and reported. For example (waybar's, ported; with
"stripSuffix" on they change nothing):
  [ { "re": "(.*) - Visual Studio Code", "to": "$1" }, { "re": "(.*) — Zen Browser", "to": "$1" } ]

Takes a list of objects. Default: [].

terminalClasses.description:
A TERMINAL'S TITLE WAITS. A shell sets the window's title to the command it is about to run and back to
the directory when it ends, so `ls` would flash "~ -> ls -> ~" across the bar. For a window of one of these
classes (whole, any case; `hyprctl clients` shows them) a title change is held "terminalTitleMs" before the
bar shows it, and a title that comes back to the one shown within it never shows. [] switches it off.

Takes a list of texts. Default: ["kitty","Alacritty","foot","footclient","org.wezfurlong.wezterm","com.mitchellh.ghostty","org.kde.konsole","konsole","XTerm","URxvt","st-256color","terminator","com.gexperts.Tilix","gnome-terminal-server","org.gnome.Terminal","org.gnome.Ptyxis","xfce4-terminal","rio","cool-retro-term"].

terminalTitleMs.description:
How long that wait is, in ms (0 to 2000; 0 = no wait): longer than a prompt takes to come back after a
quick command, short enough that a command that runs on is named at once.

Takes a whole number 0 .. 2000. Default: 150.

trayOrder.description:
The tray: an item's id (what `busctl` shows as Id: "nm-applet", "blueman").
The order of the icons: these first, in this order, then the rest as they registered.
For example ["nm-applet", "blueman"].

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

trayHide.description:
Items that are not shown at all (ids).

Takes a list of texts. Default: [].

trayRename.description:
A name for an item that does not name itself well (shown beside its icon and in its
menu), by id. For example { "nm-applet": "Network" }.

Default: {}.

openOn.description:
The tray comes out when the pointer rests on the title ("hover"), or on a click ("click": a second click puts it back).

Takes "hover" or "click". Default: "hover".

closeOnLeave.description:
Leaving it with the pointer puts it back; activating an item puts it back. true | false.

Takes true or false. Default: true.

closeOnActivate.description: Takes true or false. Default: true.

trayPassive.description:
An item that calls itself passive is "faint" | "hide" (not shown until it is active).

Takes "faint" or "hide". Default: "faint".

attention.description:
An item that wants attention shows itself beside the title: "peek" | "off".

Takes "peek" or "off". Default: "peek".

desktopText.description:
What the title says when no window has the focus.

Takes a text. Default: "Desktop".

trayIconMode.description:
"ink" draws every tray icon in the shell's own ink (legible in light and dark whatever
the icon theme ships) | "colour" draws the icons as they are.

Takes "ink" or "colour". Default: "ink".
